newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nuclear waste train sets off for dump in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Nuclear waste train sets off for dump in Germany.

text.p: Germany's biggest post-war security operation swung into action on Monday as a train carrying nuclear waste set off for a dump in the north of the country, a day after thousands of anti-nuclear activists had staged widespread protests.
Authorities banned demonstrations along the route and the shipment was to be guarded by 30,000 police.

A police spokesman said the train carrying six containers of nuclear waste left the southwestern town of Walheim early on Monday and had completed the first two and a half hours of the journey unhindered.

It was expected to reach Dannenberg in northern Germany by late afternoon, where the six containers were due to be unloaded onto a goods train and transported into Gorleben medium-term storage depot some 20 km (14 miles) away.
Thousands of people protested along the expected rail route of the spent nuclear fuel on Sunday and a bomb exploded under a railway line in central Germany.
